title: Darkness Before Closed Eyes, Then Before Open Eyes
script: This is Door 65. Darkness Before Closed Eyes, Then Before Open Eyes. It is verse 88 of the old text. In our plain words: first close the eyes and contemplate the darkness in front of them. Then open them, and spread that same dark form outward. Then, the old text says, you become one with it. Singh says this is the step from resting with the eyes closed to resting with the eyes open. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Don't press on the eyes. Simply close them. Open them slowly. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Any steady, easy position, ideally in a dim room. A chair is good. Begin with your eyes closed. [pause 4s] First, the darkness in front of your closed eyes. Rest there. Later, you will open your eyes slowly and feel the same darkness spread out in front of you, as one field. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] The darkness in front of the closed eyes. Steady. [pause 16s] Now open the eyes slowly. Feel the same darkness, spread out in front. [pause 16s] One field, inside and out. Let the count go, and rest in it. [pause 16s] Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.

title: When a Sense Is Blocked, the Void Behind It
script: This is Door 66. When a Sense Is Blocked, the Void Behind It. It is verse 89 of the old text. In our plain words: when any sense is blocked, by something from outside or on purpose, you enter an emptiness without two sides. Right there, the old text says, the Self shines. Singh says that when a sense can't reach out, a feeling of emptiness arises there, and the mind turns inward. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Use only gentle blocks: palms resting lightly over the ears, earplugs, or closed eyes. Never press on the eyes or ears. Never block the nose or mouth. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes. [pause 4s] Choose one sense. Hearing is easiest. Rest your palms lightly over your ears, or use earplugs, or simply let the eyes stay closed. Notice the empty space that opens where the sense was reaching out. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] The sense quieted. The space where it used to reach. [pause 16s] Rest in that space. Nothing to find in it. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Lower your hands whenever you like, and rest. [pause 16s] Let the breath go unwatched for a round. Move the fingers and toes. Return to the room.

title: Sounding the Plain Letter 'A'
script: This is Door 67. Sounding the plain letter 'a'. It is verse 90 of the old text. In our plain words: for one who repeats the letter 'a', with no hum at the end and no breathy ending, a great flood of knowing rises suddenly. Old readings differ on how the 'a' was sounded. This door teaches neither of the old special methods, only the plain vowel, as in 'father'. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Keep breathing naturally between sounds. Keep the voice soft. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes. [pause 4s] The sound is a plain, open 'a', as in 'father'. Not closing into a hum. Not ending in a breathy 'h'. Aloud, or in the mind. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps. On part of an out-breath, sound a soft, plain 'a', or sound it in the mind. Don't stop the breath. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] A soft, plain 'a'. Open. No ending. [pause 16s] Gently again. Rest in its open quality. [pause 16s] Let the sound rest. Let the count go. Stay in the openness it leaves. [pause 16s] Drop the exercise. Notice the room: its sounds, its light. Carry the quiet into what comes next.

title: At the End of the Out-Breathed 'Ḥ'
script: This is Door 68. At the end of the out-breathed 'ah'. It is verse 91 of the old text. In our plain words: place awareness at the very end of the soft breathy sound that closes a syllable like 'ah'. With the mind resting on nothing, the old text says, you touch the eternal. Singh explains that this soft 'h' was seen as the sound of creation going out. At its end, the mind slips into silence. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Keep the out-breath soft and easy. Take a free breath between rounds whenever you need one. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes. [pause 4s] The place to rest is the exact point where the soft 'h' at the end of 'ah' fades into silence. [pause 3s] Breathe in easily, for about four. On the out-breath, about six, sound 'ah' softly, so it ends in a gentle breathy 'h', and let it trail away with the breath. Don't stop the breath. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 20s] Follow the 'h' to its very end. Rest where it becomes silence. [pause 20s] The mind leaning on nothing. [pause 20s] Let the sound rest. Let the count go. Stay in the silence. [pause 16s] Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.

title: Oneself as Boundless Sky
script: This is Door 69. Oneself as Boundless Sky. It is verse 92 of the old text. In our plain words: meditate on yourself as having the form of the sky, with no boundary in any direction. Then, the old text says, the power of awareness, free of all support, shows its own nature. Singh describes it as resting as a vast sky, not limited by any shape or direction. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. If having no edges feels unsettling, feel the body's weight on the floor, and open your eyes. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or open them to the sky. [pause 4s] Feel yourself, not as a body in space, but as space itself. Open sky. No edge in any direction. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] Open sky. No edge. [pause 16s] Let every sense of a boundary go. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest as that openness. [pause 16s] Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.

title: Attention Gathered at the Point of a Prick
script: This is Door 70. Attention Gathered at the Point of a Prick. It is verse 93 of the old text. The school keeps this door as memory. We observe it. We do not practise it. The old text describes pricking some part of the body with a sharp needle, and joining awareness to that very spot. That, it says, is a pure passage into the divine. Singh explains the idea behind it: strong attention, from pleasure or from pain, gathers the mind to one point. The school never teaches harming the body in any way. Don't prick, pierce or hurt yourself. [pause 4s] If you want a door to practise, go to Door 1. Resting at the two turning points of the breath. This verse has no direct practice door in the school, so Door 1 is a good place to begin. There you only notice where the breath turns, at the heart and just in front of the nose. Nothing is forced, and the breath is never stopped. [pause 3s] Close the text. Take a normal breath. Look around the room and move on when ready.

title: No Inner Apparatus of Mind Within Me
script: This is Door 71. No Inner Apparatus of Mind Within Me. It is verse 94 of the old text. In our plain words: contemplate: within me there is no inner machinery of mind and the rest. Without busy thoughts, the old text says, you become free of them. Singh names that machinery: thinking mind, intellect, and the sense of ego. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. If the reflection brings confusion or unease, let it go, and simply rest with the breath. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] The reflection is: within me, there is no machinery of mind, intellect and ego. Say it quietly to yourself, once. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] No machinery of thinking within me. [pause 16s] Let the habit of being the thinking loosen. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest as the awareness that remains. [pause 16s] Drop the exercise. Notice the room: its sounds, its light. Carry the quiet into what comes next.

title: Seeing Through the Powers That Limit
script: This is Door 72. Seeing Through the Powers That Limit. It is verse 95 of the old text. In our plain words: 'Maya is what bewilders, and the limiting powers restrict.' Contemplating how these principles work, you no longer stay separate. Maya is the old name for the power that hides wholeness and shows many separate things. Singh lists her limits: on doing, knowing, wanting, time, and cause. Wallis does not count this verse as a separate practice. Singh does, so the school does too. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. This is a reflection, not a test. If it becomes heavy, let it go and rest with the breath. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] Five limits. Time. Place. What you can do. What you know. What you want. See each one as a working part of experience, not as who you are. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] Time, and place. Limits that work. Not who you are. [pause 16s] What you can do. What you know. What you want. The same. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Let the sense of being separate ease. [pause 16s] Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.

title: Letting a Desire Return to Its Source
script: This is Door 73. Letting a Desire Return to Its Source. It is verse 96 of the old text. In our plain words: seeing a desire as it suddenly arises, bring it to rest. It dissolves back into the place it came from. Singh compares desires to waves that sink back into the sea. You can practise this sitting, with any small want that appears: to move, to scratch, to check something. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. This is for ordinary wants. It is not a way to ignore real needs, like hunger, rest, or care. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or keep them soft. [pause 4s] Wait for a small want to appear. The wish to shift, to scratch, to open your eyes. Catch it at the moment it appears. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] A want appears. Look at it. Don't act. Don't fight. [pause 16s] Let it settle back where it came from. Notice the quiet there. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest in that quiet. [pause 16s] Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.

title: Who Am I Before Desire or Knowing Arise?
script: This is Door 74. Who Am I Before Desire or Knowing Arise?. It is verse 97 of the old text. In our plain words: 'When no desire, and no knowing, has arisen in me, who am I then? In truth, I am that, just as it is.' Absorbed in that, the mind becomes one with it. Wallis puts it simply: I am as I am. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Leave the question open and light. It isn't meant to be solved. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] Rest until there is a moment with no particular want and no particular thought. Then ask, quietly: who am I now? Don't answer in words. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] No want. No thought. Who am I now? [pause 16s] No answer in words. Just what is here. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest, just as it is. [pause 16s] Let the breath go unwatched for a round. Move the fingers and toes. Return to the room.

title: Desire or Knowing Seen as the Self
script: This is Door 75. Desire or Knowing Seen as the Self. It is verse 98 of the old text. In our plain words: when a desire or a thought has arisen, place the mind on it, and on nothing else, seeing it as the Self. Then comes the vision of reality. Singh says to set aside what the desire is about, and rest in the desire itself, as a power of the divine. You can practise this sitting, with any small want or thought that comes. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. This is not acting on the desire, or pushing it down. It is just resting attention in it. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or keep them soft. [pause 4s] When a small want or a thought appears, set aside what it is about. Turn to the wanting itself, the thinking itself, as energy arising in you. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] Not the object. The wanting itself. Energy arising. [pause 16s] The mind on nothing else. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest in that energy, as your own. [pause 16s] Drop the exercise. Notice the room: its sounds, its light. Carry the quiet into what comes next.

title: Thoughts Belong to No One
script: This is Door 76. Thoughts Belong to No One. It is verse 99 of the old text. In our plain words: all knowing has no fixed cause and no solid ground, and in truth it belongs to no one. One who contemplates this, the old text says, is Shiva. Singh says that when this is seen, the knower and the known fall away, and only knowing remains. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. If this view feels unsettling, go back to the ordinary sense that your thoughts are yours, and rest with the breath. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] Watch thoughts and sights and sounds arise. See each one as having no owner. They come and go, as if in open space. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] A thought arrives. No owner. It goes. [pause 16s] Like marks drifting across open space. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest as the knowing they appear in. [pause 16s] Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.

title: The Same Awareness in Every Body
script: This is Door 77. The Same Awareness in Every Body. It is verse 100 of the old text. In our plain words: the nature of awareness is present in all bodies. There is no difference anywhere. One who contemplates everything as made of it, the old text says, goes beyond the round of becoming. Singh says the same aware Self is in every being, from the highest to the tiniest. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Seeing shared awareness does not erase anyone's boundaries or needs, including your own. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] First feel the awareness in your own body. Then bring others to mind: people nearby, an animal, any living being. The same awareness in each. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] Awareness here, in this body. [pause 16s] The same in another. And another. No difference. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest in that sameness. [pause 16s] Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.

title: Stillness at the Heart of a Strong Emotion
script: This is Door 78. Stillness at the Heart of a Strong Emotion. It is verse 101 of the old text. In our plain words: in the grip of desire, anger, greed, confusion, intoxication or envy, make the mind completely still. Then the reality underneath them is all that remains. Singh says to turn from the object of the feeling to the feeling itself, neither accepting nor rejecting it. This door is for strong feelings in daily life. Sitting here, we practise only with a mild feeling that is already present, such as restlessness or boredom. Never stir up a strong one to practise. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Never bottle up feelings, and don't use this in place of getting help. If a feeling is overwhelming, or brings thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else, step away, ground yourself, and reach out to someone you trust or a local support service. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or keep them open. [pause 4s] Notice any mild feeling present now. A little restlessness. Boredom. Impatience. Set aside its story and its object. Turn to the feeling itself. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] The feeling itself. No story. Let the mind become still and soft inside it. [pause 16s] Don't act on it. Don't push it away. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Stay until only its bare energy, or quiet, remains. [pause 16s] Take a slow, free breath. Feel the feet on the ground. Then respond to the situation from the quiet, if a response is needed.

title: The World as a Magic Show or a Painting
script: This is Door 79. The World as a Magic Show or a Painting. It is verse 102 of the old text. In our plain words: for one who sees the whole universe as a magic show, or as figures in a painting, or as whirling past, happiness arises. Singh adds the picture of trees that seem to move when you watch them from a moving boat. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. Seeing the world as a show doesn't mean other people's pain is unreal. Keep care and responsibility in view. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] Recall the room around you, or your day. See it as a magic show, or a painting, or a scene passing from a boat. Vivid. But not solid. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] Vivid, but not solid. A painting. [pause 16s] A show passing by. Notice the lightness. [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest in that lightness. [pause 16s] Drop the exercise. Notice the room: its sounds, its light. Carry the quiet into what comes next.

title: Neither in Pain nor in Pleasure: What Remains Between
script: This is Door 80. Neither in Pain nor in Pleasure: What Remains Between. It is verse 103 of the old text. In our plain words: don't set the mind on pain, nor on pleasure. Let it be known what remains in the middle. Singh says what stays untouched by both, and watches both, is the real Self. [pause 3s] If it hurts, stop. This is not a way to ignore pain that needs attention or care. If you feel dizzy, restless, or a strong feeling comes up, stop. Open your eyes, and rest your attention on your feet and the floor. Find any steady, easy position. A chair is good. The floor, with a cushion under you, is good. Lying down is good. Let the floor or the chair take your weight. Close your eyes, or lower them softly. [pause 4s] Notice whatever pleasant and unpleasant feelings are here. Don't settle on either. Turn to what is in the middle, aware of both and caught by neither. [pause 3s] Breathe naturally. About four in and four out, if counting helps; if not, don't count. Don't stop the breath, and don't stretch it. Six rounds, two at a time. [pause 16s] Pleasant. Unpleasant. Neither one grasped. [pause 16s] What is in the middle? [pause 16s] Let the count go. Rest there. [pause 16s] Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.
